questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride?

options.text: In the center of your lane.
On the left side of your lane.
On the right side of your lane.
Move between all three parts of the lane as the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle increases collision risk. Riding on the far side may cause the other driver to move back into your lane too early.

questions.question: Which surface does NOT have poor traction?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, and painted lane markings all have poor traction. Dry pavement provides the best traction for motorcycle tires.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance you should keep behind another vehicle?
questions.explanation: Keep at least three seconds of distance between your motorcycle and the vehicle in front of you. More space gives you more time to react to other drivers' movements.

questions.question: What does making eye contact with other drivers mean?

options.text: It is the best way to know they see you.
It is not worth the effort.
It does not guarantee they will yield to you when they should.
It guarantees they will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not guarantee they will yield to you when they should.
questions.explanation: Do not assume eye contact means a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but do not realize they are there.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, what should you do?

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest.
Slow down as you approach it, then speed up and ride away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you approach it, then speed up and ride away.
questions.explanation: Dogs are attracted to motorcycles. If a dog chases you, downshift and slow down as you approach it. Then accelerate and ride away from it.

questions.question: The center of a lane has an oily strip from dripping vehicles. Is this safe for motorcyclists?

options.text: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
Usually safe, unless it is sunny.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: The oily strip in the lane center is usually safe when the road is dry. When wet, it can be slippery. The strip is usually less than two feet wide, so you can often ride to one side of it and still be in the center lane.

questions.question: A person convicted of DUI may receive which penalty?

options.text: Installation of a breath-alcohol device on their vehicle

questions.explanation: DUI penalties include license suspension, required breath-alcohol device installation, large fines, and community service. A warning is not a DUI penalty.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group ride?

options.text: At the front of the group
At the back of the group

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader near the front. This allows experienced riders at the back to watch them and help if needed.

questions.question: Why should you look over your shoulder before changing lanes?

options.text: Motorcycles have blind spots like other vehicles.
To make eye contact with nearby drivers

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots like other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What is the best way to be seen at an intersection?

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers
Ride close to vehicles in front of you

questions.explanation: Use your headlight to be more visible at intersections. Choose a lane position that gives oncoming traffic the best view of your motorcycle. Keep space around you to escape if needed. Do not rely on eye contact alone.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.
questions.explanation: You will rarely hear a tire go flat. A sudden change in how the motorcycle handles is a better sign of tire failure.

questions.question: In a normal turn:

options.text: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
The motorcycle and rider should lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle should lean, but the rider should not.
The rider should lean, but the motorcycle should not.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, the motorcycle and rider lean at the same angle together. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while the rider stays upright.

questions.question: The front brake supplies how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a good substitute for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: A motorcyclist can discourage other vehicles from lane sharing by:

options.text: Riding in the left portion of a lane.
Riding in the center portion of a lane.
Giving dirty looks if another driver moves into their lane.
Riding in a zigzag pattern to fill up a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in the center portion of a lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage other drivers from trying to squeeze in next to you.
